situations.label: A bill just landed on my subject
situations.note: A bill sits at authorization, the only policy stage with formal submission channels, and reading the machine view first tells you why you are arguing a clause rather than the principle.

situations.label: A consultation just opened and I want in
situations.note: A published consultation is a live opening, so this card goes straight to the board filtered to consultations. The routes for policy stage 2 are one click away from each card.

situations.label: I have a finding and nobody to send it to
situations.note: With no file, no owner and no call for submissions, you are at agenda setting, where the work is finding who should own the problem and framing it for them.

situations.label: My program or field is being evaluated
situations.note: Evaluations, audits and statutory reviews are policy stage 6, and the routes there are the evaluation unit, the reviewing committee and the Auditor General rather than the policy shop.

situations.label: A committee is studying my topic
situations.note: Most committee studies are self-initiated with no bill attached, so the leverage is in the scope and the witness list before meetings start, which is agenda setting rather than authorization.

situations.label: It is pre-budget season
situations.note: Pre-budget submissions aim at the closed room, so the routes are the two separate consultations, the minister's office and an independent cost estimate through a parliamentarian.

situations.label: Someone asked me to brief them
situations.note: A briefing request means a decision is close and a person is preparing to argue it, so the format rules of policy stage 3 apply: one page, one number, their words.

situations.label: A regulation is out for comment
situations.note: Canada Gazette Part I comment windows sit at authorization, and the routes there tell you to aim at the Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement rather than the policy in general.
